Hi all — thanks for the profile, Oliver. Below is a short technical readout and recommended footprint that balances cost and the p95 targets you outlined.

Summary and recommended topology:
- POC path (fastest): Hosted Redwood API using a reserved concurrency plan for a week of load testing. This is lowest friction and lets us collect precise latency histograms.
- Production path: Dedicated GPU pool deployed in us-west with cross-region routing fallback to us-east for DR. Use a 3-node Dedicated pool initially, node spec: 2 x NVIDIA A100-40GB per node (or equivalent Ampere), each node hosting 2 model replicas with sharded KV cache.

Sizing rationale (short prompts, p95 target <= 300 ms):
- Short prompts (<64 tokens) are latency-sensitive; with our serving runtime and a per-request batch target of 1–4 (continuous batching), two nodes (4x A100 total) should sustain ~120–160 short requests/s with p95 ~220–300 ms depending on model choice and quantization.
- To handle 140 RPS burst headroom + autoscale, 3 nodes gives comfortable buffer (sustained 250–300 short req/s), plus autoscaling to add a 4th node if sustained load > 3 mins.

Model recommendations and quantization:
- Primary model: a high-quality 13B chat model (FP16 or PTQ int8 where supported). Quantized 13B offers ~1.5–2x throughput improvement with modest quality trade-offs versus FP16 13B.
- Fallback: 6B quantized variant for steep load shedding during extreme bursts. Route by latency tolerance: UI requests -> 13B; batch scoring (lenient SLO) -> 13B or 6B depending on cost/latency.

Runtime optimizations to meet SLO:
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes (we can cache product lookup prefixes with TTL 60s).
- Aggressive continuous batching for batch scoring jobs (large batch sizes) and micro-batching for interactive requests to preserve latency.
- Kernel selection: prefer fused attention kernels for <512 tokens.

Operational runbook highlights:
- Autoscaling policy: scale-up threshold at 75% CPU/GPU utilization with cooldown 90s; scale-down after 5 mins stable under threshold.
- Monitoring: per-model p50/p95/p99, token-level cost, queue depth metric to detect backpressure.
- Fallback behavior: automatic routing to fallback 6B model when queue latency > 400 ms for 30s.

Estimated next deliverables (this week):
- Marissa: cost estimate + ops runbook (today EOD)
- Jonas: detailed node+replica config + expected latency/throughput numbers under 3 configurations (Hosted POC, Dedicated baseline, Dedicated scaled) — tomorrow morning.

I attached a quick sketch of the topology and will drop a small spreadsheet with our latency-bench numbers for 13B FP16 vs 13B int8 and 6B int8. If helpful, we can run a small closed POC on Hosted for a day to validate the 140 RPS burst profile.
